description: Signatures genuinely produced by each implementation, for the other to verify. This is the property the whole design rests on, and the only way to establish it is by execution: two implementations can each pass their own tests while disagreeing about what bytes a valid signature covers, and that disagreement is invisible until a phone and a desktop are paired.
provenance: Neither entry was hand-written. The rustProduced signature was emitted by desktop/src-tauri (ed25519-dalek) and the dartProduced one by mobile (package:cryptography), each signing the canonical payload with its own signing key. A hand-written value would prove only that someone typed 64 bytes.

sharedPayload.note: Both implementations encode these four fields to the identical bytes below. That equality is itself asserted by both suites, because a signature over a different encoding would fail for the wrong reason.

rustProduced.description: Signed by ed25519-dalek in the Rust desktop implementation, using the fixed test key from seed 1. The Dart suite verifies it.

dartProduced.description: Signed by package:cryptography in the Dart mobile implementation, using the fixed test key from seed 2. The Rust suite verifies it. A different seed from the Rust entry, so neither side can pass by accidentally verifying its own signature.
